assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational body of political-economy research linking institutions, political incentives, state capacity and fiscal policy, with broad relevance across economics.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini are central and complementary contributors to the modern field.
assessment.maturity: The theoretical and empirical consequences have been extensively developed over decades.
uncertainties: The contribution spans several closely related literatures, making a single prize formulation necessarily broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their analysis made natural capital, exhaustible resources and environmental constraints central objects of economic analysis.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal provide a highly defensible core attribution for the listed contribution.
assessment.maturity: The work is long-standing and increasingly consequential for environmental and public-policy economics.
uncertainties: The breadth of environmental economics makes the appropriate boundary of the recognized contribution contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of collateral constraints and financial amplification transformed macroeconomic accounts of credit cycles and crises.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supplied the core collateral mechanism, while Gertler is a leading contributor to its macroeconomic development.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms have been absorbed into modern macro-finance and tested against major financial episodes.
uncertainties: Credit for the broader financial-accelerator literature is diffuse, including contributors not proposed here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal-rigidity models and the New Keynesian framework supplied a durable organizing structure for monetary-policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Calvo's pricing formulation and the contributions of Woodford and Gali are central to the framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework has guided theory, empirical work and policy discussion for many years.
uncertainties: The candidate description encompasses a very large literature and more central contributors than can receive one prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Work on misallocation gave a powerful quantitative account of productivity and income differences across firms and countries.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow and Restuccia are clear principal contributors to the listed research program.
assessment.maturity: The approach has generated a large subsequent literature and important empirical applications.
uncertainties: Empirical measurement of distortions and the interpretation of residual wedges remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data made intergenerational mobility measurable at a new scale and reshaped research on opportunity and place.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are leading and closely associated contributors to this research program.
assessment.maturity: The work has produced influential findings and a substantial follow-on literature.
uncertainties: The literature is comparatively recent, and the stability and policy interpretation of the findings warrant further time.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their research clarified how technology, trade exposure and task change affect local labour markets and wage inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are strongly identified with the influential empirical research program.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been widely replicated, extended and incorporated into research and policy debate.
uncertainties: Separating causal effects of trade, technology and concurrent local adjustment remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods made forward-looking structural estimation feasible across many applied fields.
assessment.attribution: Rust is the central pioneer, with Keane a major contributor to extending and applying the approach.
assessment.maturity: The methods have had sustained influence in econometrics and quantitative economic research.
uncertainties: The intellectual lineage includes other important contributors, and structural-model credibility depends on maintained assumptions.
